# Sirach Chapter 42 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 42 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_042_page_001.jpg

---

**42:1** Do not be ashamed of these things, and do not show partiality so as to sin:

**42:2** of the law of the Most High and his covenant, and of judgment to vindicate the ungodly;

**42:3** of settling accounts with a partner and with travelers on the road, and of dividing the inheritance of a heritage;

**42:4** of the accuracy of scales and weights, and of acquiring much or little;

**42:5** of corrupt trading with merchants, and of much correction of children, and of whipping a wicked slave until he bleeds.

**42:6** A seal is good where a wicked wife is, and where there are many hands, lock things up.

**42:7** Whatever you hand over, let it be by number and weight, and the giving and receiving of everything in writing.

**42:8** Do not be ashamed to instruct the foolish and the senseless, and the one advanced in years who is judged by the young. Then you will be truly educated, and approved before all the living.

**42:9** A daughter is a hidden anxiety to a father, and worry over her robs sleep: in her youth, lest she pass the flower of her age; when married, lest she be hated;

**42:10** in her virginity, lest she be defiled and become pregnant in her father's house; when she is with a husband, lest she prove unfaithful; and when she is married, lest she be barren.

**42:11** Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, lest she make you a laughingstock to your enemies, a byword in the city and a reproach among the people, and she shame you in the assembly of the gate.

**42:12** Look at no man's beauty, and do not sit in the midst of women;

**42:13** for from a garment comes the moth, and from a woman comes the wickedness of a woman.

**42:14** Better is the wickedness of a man than a woman who does good, and a woman who brings shame and reproach.

**42:15** I will now call to remembrance the works of the Lord, and what I have seen I will declare: by the words of the Lord his works came into being.

**42:16** The shining sun looks upon all things, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory.

**42:17** The Lord has not given to holy ones the power to tell of all his wonders, which the Lord Almighty has firmly established so that the universe might stand firm in his glory.

**42:18** He searches out the deep and the heart, and understands their cunning devices; for the Most High knows all knowledge, and he looks into the sign of the age,

**42:19** declaring the things that have passed and the things that will be, and disclosing the traces of hidden things.

**42:20** No thought escapes him, and not a single word is hidden from him.

**42:21** He has set in order the glorious works of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting; nothing can be added to him, nor anything diminished, and he has no need of any counselor.

**42:22** How desirable are all his works, and how one can contemplate them even down to the spark!

**42:23** All these things live and endure forever; for every need they are all obedient to him.

**42:24** All things are in pairs, one opposite the other, and he has made nothing deficient.

**42:25** One thing establishes the good of another, and who can have enough of beholding his glory?
